N2 after N1; N1 ordered by dependency: N1-03, N1-02, N1-01. Check budgets 50/30 from the spec. Every spec default taken; no question.

discoveries.text: N1 runs N1-03 (per-op cap) before N1-02 and N1-01 on purpose: N1-01's union shadow reuses the per-op capCheck, and N1-03 retires `refused` so N1-01's two-pass memory_pr never carries the refusal branch. The ids are the spec's section names; the array order is the dependency order.

N2-02's stub case cannot be the spec's `ma` run as it stands: under auto `ma`'s facts PR is merged in its first segment, so a continue opens a fresh PR (`pr create` carries its body, no `pr edit`). The reused-PR path needs an open facts PR at the continue: the `mw` run's shape (hand-pushed harness-memory/<run>, PR opened with no tier-1 commit, left open) with a continue that adds one tier-1 fact. tests/stub-gh.sh's `STUB_GH_DOWN_ONLY` regex takes any named sub-command, so `edit` works without a stub change.

The ledger copies the whole run record to `$LEDGER/<project>/<run>/` (lib/driver.sh ledger(): `cp -r "$REC/." "$d/"`), so once N1-01 copies memory-result.json into the record, N2-03's `harness memory proposals <run>` finds it there without a new copy step.

memory_pr today merges only on the push branch (a new tier-1 commit): a reused PR with nothing new runs memory_edit alone and never memory_merge. N2-02's second continue therefore carries one more new fact so the normal push path merges after the successful edit; a merge of an already-pushed head on a bare body refresh would be a new behaviour the spec does not ask for.

Earlier runs' coding sessions on this code took 8–41 min (the 2026-11-07-2 run: builds 9–25, reviews 37–41); N1-01 is the largest feature of this run (curator.mjs, record.sh memory_pr, summary.mjs, memory-branch.sh together) and the brief fixes four features per milestone, so it may run long. The full suite was 701 s at init: a full-suite step gets a 1,500,000 ms timeout.

The brief adds one behaviour to N1-03 beyond the spec: an add that carries an anchor while ## Gotchas is under 15 and the file under 120 lines is applied as a plain add (no eviction), and the PR body (and a harness-log note, a default) name the evicted line of a real eviction as `(in place of: …)`. The `me` run at 15 Gotchas still evicts; a new unit test covers the under-cap case.

# Progress — run `agent-harness-2026-11-08` (agent-harness)

What this file is: the run's journal, rendered by the harness from `entries.jsonl`, newest entry first. One entry per session.

The run builds `docs/specs/2026-11-07-memory-followup.md`, two milestones in series. **N1**: the cap is checked per operation (a breaching op is dropped alone, `refused` retires; an anchored add under the cap is a plain add), `.claude/CLAUDE.md` and `.claude/rules/` are guarded as project memory with a memlint `twin` finding, and tier 2 lands on `harness-rules/<run>` behind a `memory rules: <run>` PR the driver never merges, counted apart in `memory.json`, the report, `ledger/memory.jsonl` and `harness memory`. **N2**: the curator session runs under `--disallowedTools Bash(git push:*) Bash(gh:*)`, `MEMORY_POLICY=auto` skips the merge after a failed body refresh, and `harness memory proposals|accept|decline <run>/<n> --why` writes `ledger/memory-answers.jsonl`, which the next curator reads and `apply` enforces.

How to read the feature list: `feature_list.json` is in priority order; a feature runs when it isn't passing and its `after` all pass. N1's features are ordered by dependency (N1-03, N1-02, N1-01, then the N1-04 review); N2 waits on all of N1. Each milestone's last feature is its Opus review, which also updates `docs/architecture.md`, `README.md` and the milestone's decision file (`journal/decisions/2026-11-08-memory-rules-pr.md`, `…-memory-session-and-answers.md`). When every feature of a milestone passes the harness verifies it and merges it into `main`.

How to steer: edit `INBOX.md` in this directory from the phone or `harness answer`. A line `status: stop <why>` or `status: pause` on top stops or pauses the run; answers to questions go under `## Answers`; a brief under the steering comment changes scope for the next session. The brief says: proceed on every default marked *default*, record them, never park.
